title.narrative: Kolkata Environmental Improvement Investment Program - Tranche 2

description.narrative: Tranche 2 will continue improvements in coverage and operational sustainability of Kolkata Municipal Corporation's sewerage, drainage, and water supply services. The accompanying TA will strengthen climate resilience of Kolkata through improved planning and disaster risk management.

Output: Sewerage and drainage extension to peripheral areas continued Indicator: By 2023, At least 83,400 additional HHs connected to S&D network (incl. FHHs) Progress/Status: Kolkata's peripheral area include Wards 101 to 144. During the period between 2015 to 2021, KMC provided building sanction in these peripheral areas to 16,975 number of properties (each having at least one drainage connection) for construction that included properties/apartments with minimum two floors (stories/levels) to multiple floors (stories/levels). As per the records of KMC, during this period KMC sanctioned at least 38,073 floors (stories/levels) in these peripheral areas. Considering that 3 number of households (HHs) per floor on an average, KMC thus, provided drainage connection to at least 114,219 HHs within the peripheral area of KMC.
All female headed households (FHHs) are covered within the sanctions accorded by KMC. Data Source: PPMS and quarterly progress reports from the PMU approved by KMC Actual value:

Service quality, operational sustainability, and climate resilience, in water supply, sewerage and drainage in the service area of KMC increased

KMC's Water Supply Department's operation and maintenance cost recovery maintained at 100%; (2015 baseline: 100%) Progress/Status: 104% of operation and maintenance cost recovered during financial year 2020-21 Data Source: KMC's Water Department's annual reports Actual value:

At least 76,500 HHs in pilot areas (East Kolkata and Joka) received 24x7 treated water supply (incl. est. 167,000 females) (2015 baseline: 7-8 hours per day on average in East Kolkata and 4 hours per day on average in Joka) Progress/Status: This project has developed the distribution network for the 24x7 treated water supply in the pilot areas of East Kolkata and Joka. KMC is separately working on the augmentation of the supply of water to the network, where the work is under progress. Once, the supply augmentation is complete, the area would receive 24x7 treated water supply, which will ensure supply to more than the target 76,500 HHs. Data Source: KMC's Water Department's annual reports Actual value:

By 2023, At least 843,500 HHs in KMC's service area received treated water for a minimum of 12 hours per day (incl. est. 1.95 million females) (2015 baseline: 7-8 hours per day on average) Progress/Status: To date KMC is able to provide treated water to about 801,000 HHs for about 10 to 11 hours and to about 42,000 HHs (in the project area spreading over Ward 001 to Ward 006, after the implementation of work on NRW) for about 20 to 22 hours a day. On a weighted average basis, KMC is able to provide treated water to about all the target 843,500 HHs for more than 12 hours/day.
KMC expects that this will improve further as the impact of NRW exercise is scaled up in other Wards of KMC on a gradual basis. Data Source: KMC's Water Department's annual reports Actual value:
